headline.technical: CNBC reported Wall Street hammered Alphabet over an earnings miss, while Brent closed at 110.00 (1d -4.61%) and the ECB said Lagarde will step down on 7 February 2027.
headline.layman: Google's parent company disappointed investors, oil prices fell but stay high, and the head of Europe's central bank said she will step down next year.

global.title: AI-spending doubts hit tech; oil eases but stays high

status.technical: The Financial Times reported the Nasdaq 100 set to open 1% down after Alphabet and Microsoft reported lower than expected capex. Brent closed at 110.00 (1d -4.61%). S&P 500 closed 7743.98 on 2026-10-28, 1d 0.28%. VIX closed 16.97.
status.layman: The Financial Times reported that US tech shares were set to open lower after Google's parent and Microsoft reported spending that was lower than expected. Oil fell but is still very high.

consequence.technical: Economic Times reported investors increasingly favour tech firms showing financial discipline in AI. If that persists, heavy AI spenders may lag firms with strong cash flow. Bloomberg said credit default swaps show growing risk in data-center bonds.
consequence.layman: Economic Times reported investors now want to see returns on AI spending. If that continues, companies that spend carefully may be rewarded more than big spenders.

impact.technical: Tech and AI-linked shares, and holders of data-center bonds (Bloomberg). Energy firms benefit: the FT reported Shell, TotalEnergies and Repsol posted a surge in third-quarter earnings. WSJ reported euro-area businesses and consumers face pressure from elevated energy prices.
impact.layman: Tech investors and people holding AI-related bonds are affected. Oil companies are earning a lot more, while households and firms in Europe feel the cost of expensive energy.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the S&P 500 rose the next day 54% of 845 times (median 0.09%) and over the next 5 days 59% of 843 times (median 0.38%).
outlook.layman: This is only history, not a forecast: after calm days like this, the S&P 500 rose the next day 54% of the time and over the next five days 59% of the time.

regions.title: Americas: tech slides after Alphabet earnings

status.technical: WSJ reported Nasdaq futures slumped after Google earnings disappointed; the FT said the Nasdaq 100 was set to open 1% down. Nasdaq Composite closed 26549.85 on 2026-10-28, 1d 0.27%; S&P 500 1d 0.28%.
status.layman: WSJ reported that tech-heavy US futures fell after Google's earnings disappointed. Before that, US stocks had closed slightly higher.

consequence.technical: CNBC reported weaker-than-expected revenue in Alphabet's core business. If investors read that as AI taking a bite out of search, as CNBC put it, pressure on AI-exposed names could continue.
consequence.layman: If investors decide AI is eating into Google's search business, as CNBC suggested, other AI-linked shares could stay under pressure.

impact.technical: Economic Times reported Alphabet shares plunged while Microsoft and Oracle gained on strong cash flow prospects, so effects within tech are uneven.
impact.layman: Google's parent fell sharply, but Economic Times said Microsoft and Oracle gained, so not all tech was hit.

outlook.layman: Only history, not a forecast: after calm days, the Nasdaq rose the next day 55% of the time and over five days 59% of the time.

regions.title: Europe: energy and aerospace lift shares before ECB

status.technical: Economic Times reported European shares edged higher as energy and aerospace gains offset tech weakness, with Shell and Airbus advancing after earnings. DAX closed 25951.62 (1d 0.96%), FTSE 100 10730.73 (1d 0.34%), Euro Stoxx 50 6185.45 (1d 0.29%).
status.layman: Economic Times reported European shares edged up, helped by energy and aerospace companies, while tech was weak. Investors were waiting for the European Central Bank's decision.

consequence.technical: Bloomberg and the ECB said Lagarde will step down on 7 February 2027. WSJ said this comes as debt problems and resurgent inflation are looming. Bloomberg flagged a rate decision ahead; the outcome is not in the notes.
consequence.layman: The head of the ECB said she will leave in February 2027. WSJ said this comes as debt worries and rising prices loom. A rate decision was due, and the notes do not say what it was.

impact.technical: WSJ reported eurozone economic sentiment fell again in October on elevated energy prices, and German consumers grew slightly gloomier. Reuters reported Haleon cut its outlook.
impact.layman: WSJ reported that confidence among European consumers and businesses fell again because energy is expensive.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the Euro Stoxx 50 rose the next day 53% of 851 times (median 0.06%) and over 5 days 56% of 849 times (median 0.36%).
outlook.layman: Only history, not a forecast: after calm days, the Euro Stoxx 50 rose the next day 53% of the time and over five days 56% of the time.

regions.title: Asia-Pacific: tech selloff in China and Korea, Japan gains

status.technical: Economic Times reported the Shanghai Composite fell 0.9%, the CSI300 dropped 1.2% and the STAR50 tumbled 4.2% on a tech and AI selloff. KOSPI fell 2.18% as Samsung Electronics dropped 4.13% after disappointing third-quarter profits. Investing.com reported the Nikkei 225 up 1.00% at close.
status.layman: Economic Times reported Chinese tech and AI shares fell sharply. South Korea's market dropped after Samsung Electronics reported disappointing profits. Japan's market closed higher.

consequence.technical: Economic Times reported Korean authorities pledged to monitor volatility. SCMP quoted analysts saying massive state buying will be insufficient to engineer a durable rally in China. Past this, the notes give no firm reason for further moves.
consequence.layman: Analysts quoted by SCMP said government buying alone is unlikely to produce a lasting rally in China. Korean authorities said they would watch volatility.

impact.technical: Chinese tech and AI-related shares and Samsung Electronics were the main drags in the notes; Economic Times said Korean losses extended across battery, automotive and steel stocks.
impact.layman: Chinese tech and Samsung were the weak spots; Korean battery, car and steel shares also fell.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the Nikkei 225 rose the next day 54% of 822 times (median 0.08%) and over 5 days 57% of 819 times (median 0.45%).
outlook.layman: Only history, not a forecast: after calm days, Japan's Nikkei rose the next day 54% of the time and over five days 57% of the time.

status.technical: Bloomberg reported oil declined as traders parsed signs of fresh diplomacy on Iran. Brent closed at 110.00 (1d -4.61%, 1m 6.25%); WTI closed at 101.18. WSJ asked why prices remain above $100 a barrel.
status.layman: Bloomberg reported oil fell on signs of new talks over Iran, but WSJ noted prices are still above $100 a barrel.

consequence.technical: Reuters reported TSX futures climbed as the oil retreat eased inflation fears. If oil stays high, Business Standard said it fuels bets on another RBI rate hike in December.
consequence.layman: Reuters said lower oil eased worries about rising prices. If oil stays high, Business Standard said India's central bank may raise rates again.

impact.technical: FT reported oil majors lifted buybacks on bumper profits; Shell's refining margin hit a record US$42 a barrel (Straits Times). Fuel buyers and energy-importing economies face higher costs.
impact.layman: Oil companies are making record profits. People and countries that buy fuel pay more.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day falls this large, Brent rose over the next 5 days 54% of 168 times (median 0.39%), with a wide 10th-90th range of -6.13% to 7.21%.
outlook.layman: Only history, not a forecast: after big one-day oil falls, oil rose over the next five days 54% of the time, with wide swings either way.

drivers.title: AI financing and investor demands for returns

status.technical: Economic Times reported Wall Street favours AI spenders with financial discipline. Bloomberg reported credit default swaps show growing risk in data-center bonds and asked whether investors have bought all the AI bonds they can handle. WSJ reported bankers sound cautious about the AI boom.
status.layman: Reporters at Economic Times, Bloomberg and WSJ all pointed to growing caution about paying for the AI boom.

consequence.technical: Bloomberg raised the question of whether AI wobbles were part of the Fed's calculation to keep rates on hold. If AI financing strains grow, rate decisions could be affected; the notes do not confirm this.
consequence.layman: Bloomberg asked whether AI worries helped the Fed keep rates unchanged. That is a question, not a confirmed fact.

impact.technical: Holders of data-center bonds and AI-heavy tech stocks are the most exposed in the notes; evidence on wider effects is thin.
impact.layman: AI-linked bonds and tech shares are most exposed; the notes say little about wider effects.

outlook.technical: Base rates are in the index lines, not for AI financing itself, so no historical outlook is offered here; these are not predictions.
outlook.layman: There is no historical pattern in the data for this topic, so no outlook is given.

drivers.title: Central banks: Fed hold, ECB leadership, BOJ and RBI

status.technical: CNBC reported Treasury yields eased after the Fed rate hold. US 10-year yield closed 5.05 (1d 1.04%). WSJ reported a BOJ rate hold seen as a done deal, with focus on guidance. Lagarde to step down 7 February 2027 (ECB).
status.layman: The Fed kept rates unchanged and bond yields eased, CNBC reported. The Bank of Japan was expected to hold rates too.

consequence.technical: CNBC analysis said Warsh made clear he leans toward higher interest rates but left himself options depending on data. Emkay expects the RBI to raise rates by 75 basis points by February 2027, per Mint.
consequence.layman: CNBC said the new Fed chief leans toward higher rates but is keeping options open. Emkay, quoted by Mint, expects India to raise rates.

impact.technical: Mint reported the Fed hold gave temporary support to Indian equities, though elevated oil and tighter domestic policy could limit gains.
impact.layman: Mint said the Fed hold helped Indian shares for now, but high oil and higher local rates could limit gains.

outlook.technical: Base rates not provided for central-bank decisions; these are not predictions.
outlook.layman: No historical pattern is provided for this topic, so no outlook is given.

events.technical: Economic Times said markets expect the BOJ to hold rates steady; WSJ said the focus is on guidance.
events.layman: Japan's central bank is expected to keep rates unchanged, with attention on what it says next.

events.title: Lagarde's departure from the ECB
events.technical: Bloomberg reported Lagarde will resign effective this date; FT said her term was set to end in October 2027.
events.layman: The head of Europe's central bank will leave on this date, earlier than planned.

companyEffects.layman: Google's parent missed expectations and its shares fell, weighing on tech.

companyEffects.layman: Reports differ: lower spending than expected, but Economic Times said its shares gained.

companyEffects.technical: Economic Times reported Airbus advanced after its earnings update, helping offset tech weakness in Europe.
companyEffects.layman: Airbus shares rose after its results.

companyEffects.layman: Samsung fell after weak profits and dragged South Korea's market down.

companyEffects.layman: TotalEnergies posted record profit and plans to pay shareholders more.
